claims.text: The investigated Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni quinary alloy and selected equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after thermomechanical processing.
Changing the constituent elements alters local lattice distortion.
Differences in constituent atomic radii cause variation in local lattice distortion.
Variation in local lattice distortion governs mechanical-property differences among these alloys.
Local lattice distortion affects dislocation mobility.
Distortion-induced changes in dislocation mobility alter deformation behavior.
Changes in deformation behavior produce differences in mechanical properties.
Alloys with greater local lattice distortion will have higher strength than the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline.
Alloys with greater local lattice distortion will have lower ductility than the equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni baseline.
The proposed relationship applies to single-phase FCC alloys whose constituent elements have significant atomic-radius differences.
The exact relationship between local lattice distortion and mechanical properties is not well established.
The proposed experiment will compare constituent-varied alloys with the equiatomic quinary baseline under room-temperature uniaxial tensile loading.
